title: Tell stuck requests from idle workers in a thread snapshot

blocks.text: The payments service has an admin page that sorts the JVM's threads into three groups: **active**, **idle**, and **stuck behind another thread**. During the last incident it showed 0 stuck, while every payment request was waiting for one thread to finish, and on-call restarted the service without looking further. On a quiet night, it must not call the idle mailer workers stuck either.
The page reads a snapshot from `ThreadMXBean.getThreadInfo(...)`, and `ThreadTriage` already counts and groups the threads. Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/ThreadTriage.java`:

items: `classify(ThreadInfo thread)`: which of the three activities this thread is in.

blocks.text: A thread is stuck behind another when it can't go on until another thread lets go of something it holds; `stuckBehind` then reports it under that thread's name. About three lines in total.
The tests start real threads, put each one somewhere (computing, in a lock, in a queue, in a sleep) and hand your method the snapshot `ThreadMXBean` takes of them.

cases.says: threads queued to enter a synchronized block are stuck behind the thread inside it, which is active, and a sleeping thread is idle
threads waiting for a ReentrantLock are stuck behind the thread that holds it
workers waiting in a queue or on a latch are idle, not stuck
a thread waiting for a lock with a timeout is stuck behind the holder while it waits

origin.section: BLOCKED Means Waiting for a synchronized Monitor; a Thread Waiting for a ReentrantLock Is WAITING

concepts: BLOCKED means waiting to enter or re-enter a synchronized monitor; a thread waiting for a ReentrantLock, a semaphore, a latch or a queue is parked and shows WAITING or TIMED_WAITING.

Whether a waiting thread is stuck behind another is told by what it waits for and who holds it, not by its state: an idle worker in take() and a request parked on a held ReentrantLock are both WAITING.
WAITING and TIMED_WAITING differ only in whether the wait has a timeout; neither says whether the thread is in another thread's way or holds a lock.
